# Proper filters extend to prime filters

Let $F$ be a proper [filter](prime-filters-of-a-heyting-algebra.md) in a Heyting algebra $H$ and $a \in H$ with $a \notin F$. Then there is a prime filter $G$ with $F \subseteq G$ and $a \notin G$.

**Proof sketch.** By Zorn's lemma the filters that contain $F$ and omit $a$, ordered by inclusion, have a maximal element $G$. If $b \cup c \in G$ with $b, c \notin G$, the filters generated by $G \cup \{b\}$ and $G \cup \{c\}$ both contain $a$, so $a \ge g \cap b$ and $a \ge g' \cap c$ for some $g, g' \in G$; then $a \ge (g \cap g') \cap (b \cup c) \in G$ by distributivity, a contradiction. The maximal element need not be a maximal proper filter.
